page: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-4 is a graphics-optimized virtual machine belonging to the g2 family. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon CPU with 4 dedicated vCPUs, consisting of 2 physical cores and 2 threads per core, operating at a base speed of 2.2 GHz. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB per core, and does not include local storage.

The defining hardware component of this server is a single NVIDIA L4 GPU based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, featuring 24 GB of dedicated VRAM. This GPU enables high-performance acceleration for parallel computing tasks, specifically machine learning and graphics processing.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between CPU and GPU capabilities. Standard CPU-bound operations, such as stress-ng multi-core performance, Geekbench scores, and Redis operations, fall into the bottom 25% tier. However, the GPU-accelerated LLM inference benchmarks for small (135M) and medium (7B) models rank in the top 10% tier for both prompt processing and text generation.

This resource distribution offers a cost-effective profile for projects requiring GPU acceleration without the overhead of high-tier CPU and memory allocations. It is highly suited for small to medium LLM inference, graphics rendering, and lightweight machine learning workloads, though it is less optimal for CPU-heavy or memory-intensive non-GPU tasks.
description: Google Cloud Platform g2-standard-4 is a graphics-optimized server designed for GPU-accelerated workloads. It features an Intel Xeon x86_64 CPU with 4 dedicated vCPUs, 16.0 GB of system memory, and no local storage. The system's primary accelerator is a single NVIDIA L4 GPU from the Ada Lovelace family, equipped with 24 GB of VRAM. While standard CPU and memory benchmarks place this instance in the lower performance tiers, its GPU-driven capabilities excel in machine learning tasks. Specifically, LLM inference benchmarks for small and medium models rank in the top 10% for both prompt processing and text generation. This configuration provides a cost-effective entry point for parallel computing workloads, making it highly suitable for lightweight AI inference, graphics rendering, and GPU-based development, while avoiding the expense of over-provisioned CPU and system memory resources.
